name: Aeracura

attributes.attribute: paired with Dis Pater on a statue at Oberseebach
male form of Aeracura, recorded in Northumberland
may descend from an earth goddess

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Aeracura, also called Aericura or Heracura, was a Celtic goddess. People worshipped her in Germany and Switzerland. A stone statue at Oberseebach in Switzerland pairs her with Dis Pater. People also venerated her near Stuttgart in Germany. Her name sounds like that of the Greek goddess Hecate, so scholars connect the two. She may have begun as an earth goddess whom Dis Pater pushed aside. A male form, Aericurus, appears in records from Northumberland. Art shows Aeracura holding a cornucopia. That emblem stands for fruitfulness and for the Otherworld. The book also places her with the Deae Matres.

okr.objective: Record the goddess Aeracura, her emblems, her partners, and her lands of worship.
key_results: Identify Aeracura as a goddess of Germany and Switzerland.
Show her statues at Oberseebach and near Stuttgart and her male form Aericurus.
Note her links to Hecate, Dis Pater, and the Deae Matres.
